solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Compliment and regularly laud Slough (6)

indicators.note: at regular intervals: every other letter

blocks.note: a slough is a bog, a mire

annotation.surface: Someone praising and lauding the Berkshire town of Slough, not an obvious object of admiration.
annotation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London famous for being unlovely, and the capital hides its role as the plain noun for a bog.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: to compliment is to praise, and admire can mean to express admiration aloud.

entries.clue: Reach home, full of love and aspiration (8)

indicators.note: the word for home is filled with the letter for love

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, O

annotation.surface: Coming home full of love and hope: a happy homecoming.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reach home' reads as arriving at the house, but it is two separate pieces: AMBIT, then I(O)N.
annotation.definitionFit: Ambition is aspiration, the desire to achieve something.

entries.clue: Woman’s focus: get rid of long whiskers (9)

definitions.note: whiskers is plural; a moustache is a single growth of whiskers

indicators.note: the focus of a word is its centre letter

blocks.note: to oust is to get rid of
to long for is to ache for

annotation.surface: A woman determined to remove some unwanted long whiskers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Long whiskers' looks like one phrase describing the definition, but 'long' is the verb ACHE and only 'whiskers' defines.
annotation.definitionFit: A moustache is the whiskers grown on the upper lip.

entries.clue: Raving of guy on Ecstasy (4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next

blocks.note: to guy someone is to mock or rag them

annotation.surface: A man ranting wildly while high on ecstasy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is not a man here but the verb to guy, to tease, which is RAG.
annotation.definitionFit: Raving and rage both mean wild, furious talk or anger.

entries.clue: “Dead end” clued as “bum, cold” (3-2-3)

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters are wrongly arranged

blocks.note: C for cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A setter admitting that the clue for 'dead end' came out as a bum, cold one.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue talks about itself: the words 'clued as' are the letters, and 'bum' is the adjective meaning dud, not the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym borrowed from French: a street closed at one end, literally 'bottom of the bag'.

entries.clue: Opens sensual novel (7)

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

annotation.surface: Someone opening a steamy romance novel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sensual novel' reads as a racy book; 'novel' is the adjective meaning new, telling you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: To unseal something is to open it.

entries.clue: Disconsolate old man wanting hugs (10)

indicators.note: the outer word wraps its arms round the inner one

blocks.note: your old man is your father, PA

annotation.surface: A lonely old man, miserable for lack of affection.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' looks like it means lacking, which fits the sad surface, but it is DESIRING, which hugs PA.
annotation.definitionFit: Disconsolate and despairing both mean without hope or comfort.

entries.clue: Bottom of cavernous cistern smelt bad (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a cistern is a water tank

annotation.surface: The bottom of a big old cistern gave off a foul smell.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottom of' works because in a down clue the last letter sits at the bottom of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Stank is the past tense of stink, to smell bad.

entries.clue: Starts to cap abnormally square tooth (6)

indicators.note: take the first letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: first letters of Cap and Abnormally
nine is a square number, three times three

annotation.surface: A dentist starting to cap an oddly square tooth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Square tooth' reads as a shape, but 'square' is a square number: NINE.
annotation.definitionFit: A canine is the pointed tooth between the incisors and the premolars.

entries.clue: Pester Head of History, a right idiot (6)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A teacher badgering the Head of History, whom they think a complete idiot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head of History' reads as a school job title, but it only gives the letter H.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to keep bothering someone.

entries.clue: Sad person singing country music (9)

blocks.note: in British slang a grass is an informer, and to sing is to inform to the police

annotation.surface: A melancholy singer performing country music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Person singing' looks like a vocalist, but in British criminal slang to sing is to inform, and an informer is a GRASS.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the banjo-and-fiddle style from Kentucky is one kind of country music.

entries.clue: Cross about wife and kids (5)

indicators.note: the first word goes round the second

blocks.note: to span a river is to cross it

annotation.surface: An angry man complaining about his wife and children.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' sits in the surface as the adjective for angry, but it is the verb, SPAN.
annotation.definitionFit: Spawn is a disparaging word for offspring, a person's kids.

entries.clue: See you in Egypt, at Aswan (2-2)

indicators.note: the answer is inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A traveller saying goodbye somewhere in Egypt, at Aswan on the Nile.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma is only there for the surface; read straight through it.
annotation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British goodbye, like see you.

entries.clue: Barmy relatives providing element of slapstick (6,4)

annotation.surface: A mad family putting on some knockabout comedy.
annotation.walkthrough: The split falls inside BANANA'S: the S belongs to BANANAS, not to SKIN.
annotation.definitionFit: Slipping on a banana skin is the classic slapstick gag.

entries.clue: Liberal radicals probing extremely frustrating stealth tax (6,4)

indicators.note: liberal means free, so the letters are freely rearranged
the rearranged letters probe into, go inside, the other piece
take the extreme letters, the first and last

blocks.note: first and last letters of FrustratinG

annotation.surface: Political commentary: radical Liberals looking into a frustrating hidden tax.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Liberal radicals' looks like a party faction; 'Liberal' is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Fiscal drag is the extra tax raised when thresholds are not raised with inflation, a tax rise nobody announces.

entries.clue: Centre of Cork carpeted with small flowers (7)

indicators.note: the centre of a four-letter word is its middle two letters

blocks.note: the middle two letters of cORk
carpeted means told off; chid is an old past tense of chide

annotation.surface: A room in the middle of Cork carpeted and decorated with small flowers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carpeted' means reprimanded (to be carpeted is to be summoned and scolded), and CHID is the old past tense of chide.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the orchid family is one of the largest groups of flowering plants.

entries.clue: Season sprout well (6)

blocks.note: to sprout is to shoot up suddenly, a verb
a well is a source of water rising from the ground, a noun

annotation.surface: Seasoning some sprouts nicely.
annotation.walkthrough: There are three definitions here, not two: season, sprout and well each give SPRING.
annotation.definitionFit: Spring is a season, a verb meaning to sprout, and a source of water like a well.

entries.clue: Audibly disparaged one exiting male toilet, active at night (9)

indicators.note: the word is to be heard, not read
the I leaves the word it was in

blocks.note: to knock something is to disparage it
URINAL, a men's toilet, without I (one)

annotation.surface: Someone bad-mouthing a man leaving the gents during the night.
annotation.walkthrough: The male toilet is URINAL, and 'one' is the Roman numeral I, which leaves it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym phrased as a description, the way a dictionary glosses owls and bats.

entries.clue: Austrian novice on slope (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

annotation.surface: An Austrian beginner skier on the nursery slope.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slope' pulls towards the ski slope, but it is the verb, LEAN.
annotation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is a region of Austria, so Tyrolean is Austrian.

entries.clue: Bond’s boss spies on monarch in old kingdom (6)

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed after

blocks.note: the CIA, the US spy agency

annotation.surface: A spy chief keeping the king under surveillance in some ancient realm.
annotation.walkthrough: The spies come first in the clue but go second: 'on monarch' puts them after ER.
annotation.definitionFit: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the English Midlands.

entries.clue: Attack lieutenant south of Caribbean capital, not north (7)

indicators.note: a down clue reads like a map with north at the top, so south of means placed underneath
remove the letter that follows

blocks.note: NASSAU, capital of the Bahamas, without N

annotation.surface: A military order: attack the lieutenant south of a Caribbean capital.
annotation.walkthrough: Nassau is the capital of the Bahamas; dropping its N (north) leaves ASSAU, with LT placed below.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, noun or verb: a violent attack, or to attack someone.

entries.clue: Lauda broadcast on motor racing in particular (7)

indicators.note: the name is heard over the air, not spelt
in an across clue, placed after

blocks.note: Formula One, F1, with the 1 as I
Niki Lauda, the Austrian racing driver

annotation.surface: Commentary on Niki Lauda, a famously meticulous Formula One driver.
annotation.walkthrough: Niki Lauda was a three-time Formula One world champion, so the surface is all F1. The 1 of F1 stands in as the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: Finicky means fussy, particular about details.

entries.clue: Officers at law periodically left for holiday (6)

indicators.note: every other letter is what is left after the rest go

blocks.note: the even letters of oFfIcErS aT lAw

annotation.surface: Police officers taking time off for a holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' does not mean the side; the letters left, once every other one is gone, spell the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a holiday or festival, especially in Spain.

entries.clue: Ascending part of intestine containing last of enormous breakfast (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means read bottom to top
the reversed word holds the extra letter
the last of a word is literally its final letter, the one that comes last

blocks.note: the ILEUM, part of the small intestine, reversed

annotation.surface: A huge breakfast working its way through the gut.
annotation.walkthrough: The ileum is the last stretch of the small intestine.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the oat-and-fruit cereal is a typical breakfast.

entries.clue: Left in peace, played solemn duet (10)

indicators.note: the letters are played in a different order

annotation.surface: Two musicians given peace and quiet to perform a solemn duet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Played' belongs to the musical surface, but here it tells you to rearrange the letters of 'solemn duet'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in its older sense: molest once meant simply to bother, so unmolested is undisturbed.

entries.clue: Second balls-up in career (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word reads upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
balls is nonsense, ROT, turned upward

annotation.surface: A second blunder in someone's working life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Balls-up' is British slang for a mess, but here it splits: balls is ROT, and 'up' turns it round. 'Career' is the verb, to rush along.
annotation.definitionFit: To career along is to speed along, to motor.

entries.clue: Lord in court over game (4)

blocks.note: a British barrister addresses the judge as 'm'lud'
O for over, the cricket scoring abbreviation

annotation.surface: A judge presiding over a game in court.
annotation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket, abbreviated O on scorecards.
annotation.definitionFit: Ludo is a board game played with dice and counters.

entries.clue: Characters leading open rebellion, chasing abominable whale (4)

indicators.note: the characters that lead each word are the first letters

blocks.note: first letters of Open Rebellion Chasing Abominable

annotation.surface: Rebel leaders in open revolt, hunting a monstrous whale, like Captain Ahab.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abominable' nudges towards the snowman, but it is just another word supplying its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the killer whale is the largest of the dolphins, loosely called a whale.

entries.clue: Half-cut saps finally get your goat (5)

indicators.note: half of the word is cut off
finally means at the end, so the letter that comes at the end of the word

blocks.note: yr is the abbreviation for your

annotation.surface: Drunken fools finally annoying you: half-cut is British slang for drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get your goat' is the idiom for annoy, but 'goat' alone is the definition; 'half-cut' means drunk as well as halved.
annotation.definitionFit: A satyr is a mythical half-man, half-goat.

entries.clue: Statement from unqualified civil engineer following article (9)

indicators.note: the engineer comes after the article

annotation.surface: A statement issued by an unqualified civil engineer after an article about them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unqualified' looks like lacking qualifications, but it means absolute: UTTER.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are something put into words.

entries.clue: Irish capital both sides of the water (8)

indicators.note: the letters on each side of the word, its first and last

blocks.note: first and last letters of ThE

annotation.surface: Dublin, the Irish capital, straddling the River Liffey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Irish capital' looks like Dublin; it is two pieces, IR and a different capital, RIGA.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb, used of supplying fields with water through channels.

entries.clue: Cycling along after drinking fifty eight pints (6)

indicators.note: letters go round: the last letter moves to the front
the cycled word takes the other letter inside it

blocks.note: ALONG with its G cycled to the front
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

annotation.surface: A cyclist stopping along the way to drink eight pints.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eight pints' is a quantity, not a drinking session: a gallon is eight pints.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the imperial and US gallon each hold eight of their own pints.
